There are 60 minutes in an hour.

Streamline Autos' direct-to-consumer (DTC) strategy for their electric vehicle range poses a significant competitive threat and necessitates a strategic response from our business. By bypassing traditional dealership networks, they are leveraging cost efficiencies to offer more competitive pricing, which directly pressures our price points and margin structures. Furthermore, their model allows for direct engagement with customers, providing them with first-party data on consumer behavior and preferences. This data advantage enables them to iterate on product features, marketing messages, and customer experience more rapidly than competitors reliant on third-party dealerships.

The implications for our business are twofold. First, we face increased pressure to justify our pricing through superior value propositions, such as enhanced after-sales service, financing options, or brand loyalty programs. Second, we must accelerate our own digital transformation efforts to capture direct customer insights. If we remain dependent solely on traditional dealership networks, we risk falling behind in understanding real-time market demands. To mitigate this, we should consider integrating more direct digital touchpoints, enhancing our online sales capabilities, and leveraging our existing dealer relationships to provide them with better data tools, thereby turning them into partners in customer insight rather than just sales channels.
